headline: Tools and benchmarks refine annotation of repeats, isoforms and polyadenylation sites
label: Genome And Transcript Annotation Methods
summary: Long-read, direct RNA and small-RNA sequencing now yield annotated features whose accuracy depends heavily on the chosen annotation method.
synthesis: The common thread is that annotation outputs, rather than raw sequence, are becoming the object of scrutiny in genomics. A benchmark of five nanopore direct RNA annotation tools (StringTie3, IsoQuant, Bambu, FLAIR, FLAMES) on net blotch-infected barley reports variable isoform annotation across methods. A pangenome study shows that gene presence-absence variation often reflects annotation method differences rather than sequence differences, with cotton as a case study. PolyAseqTrap provides genome-wide identification and quantification of polyadenylation sites across diverse 3' end sequencing data, while piRAT annotates primary piRNAs from clusters and secondary piRNAs via ping-pong cycles. AniAnns, a preprint, applies alignment-free average nucleotide identity between repeat units to annotate tandem repeat arrays and satellite DNA. Across these items, the methodological advance is toward alignment-free or cross-tool frameworks that make feature annotation more comparable and reproducible.
